description: 18 public tasks: six coding, six writing, six combined. Combined tasks reuse the six coding scenarios; these are not 18 independent problem samples. Only the invoice fixture reproduces a recorded specialist hire; other repository fixtures are deliberately broken reconstructions.

origin.kind: exact recorded hire seed and recovered solution

invoice-contract.kind: contract and sanitized summary of recorded hire
invoice-contract.text:
INVOICE CONTRACT. invoiceBalance(invoiceCents, payments) returns invoice amount minus unique payments. Amounts are integer cents; negative payment amounts are refunds and a negative balance is a credit. Invoice must be a nonnegative safe integer. Every payment must have a nonempty, non-whitespace string ref and a safe-integer cents value; invalid entries throw TypeError. Validate each entry, even a repeat. Reference equality is exact and case-sensitive: do not trim or lowercase references. An identical reference/amount pair counts once; the same reference with a different amount throws TypeError. Different references with the same amount are separate payments. Do not mutate caller data. For this fixture the input is an array and all intermediate totals are within the safe-integer range.
Recorded origin: a buyer agent asked a remote specialist to repair this synthetic invoice repository. The recovered repair passed buyer-side checks, but the initial automatic commit/push failed and an operator recovered the work. It is a real delegation attempt on a synthetic repository, not evidence of a production customer incident or a matched baseline advantage.

mentions-contract.text: MENTION CONTRACT. mentionedNames(content) receives a string. Recognize @ followed by one or more ASCII letters, digits, underscore or hyphen. The @ must be at the beginning or preceded by a character other than an ASCII word character, @ or slash. Return lowercase names in first-seen order, once each. Empty input returns []. Do not summon names from email addresses, embedded word fragments, /@paths or @@double-at syntax. Punctuation and line breaks may precede a valid mention. This fixture does not resolve names to pubkeys and does not implement Unicode usernames. In Fez the downstream addressing event needs the resolved p tag; highlighting text alone does not deliver a message.

author-contract.text:
AUTHOR CONTRACT. authorAllowed({mode, allowlist, author, owner, isSibling}) must return a boolean. author and allowlist entries are strings; owner is a string or undefined. Normalize these keys by trimming and lowercasing. Empty author always fails. Exact mode 'anyone' allows any nonempty author. Other modes admit owner OR an allowlisted collaborator OR isSibling === true; they otherwise fail closed. An unknown mode does not become public. A missing owner alone grants no access, but an explicitly verified sibling or allowlisted collaborator still qualifies. allowlist is an additive array, not a replacement for owner access. No input mutation.
The caller computes isSibling from the owner's verified attestation. This pure fixture does not verify signatures or establish sibling status, and a stranger's textual claim must not count as that boolean. In the real system the workspace roster and the agent's author policy are separate checks.

history-contract.text: HISTORY CONTRACT. mergeHistory(cached, page) receives arrays of already-verified events {id:string, ts:number} and page={events, failed:boolean}. An id identifies an immutable event; repeated IDs have identical content in these fixtures. Return {messages, status, partial}. Merge cached and page events by exact ID, keep one of each, and order ascending by ts then lexically by id. Never mutate caller arrays or events. If failed is true, status is 'error' and partial is true exactly when any merged messages exist. A successful page yields status 'ready' and partial false, even when empty. Success must retain cached messages. This narrow fixture does not implement pagination cursors, signature verification, relay transport or channel membership.

handoff-contract.text:
HANDOFF CONTRACT. makeHandoff(original, pick, roster) receives the original request string, a model pick object or null, and a roster of {name:string, available:boolean}. Return {to: name, task: original} only when pick.agent exactly matches an available roster name. Return null for an absent pick, unknown name or unavailable specialist. Name matching is case-sensitive. Preserve the original request byte-for-byte as a JS string, including newlines and constraints; ignore any pick.task summary. Do not rewrite input objects or infer names from message content. This does not transmit anything; the actual Fez transport is outside the fixture.
This is intentionally a small control task: a direct solution can be excellent, and unnecessary delegation may only add delay.

delivery-contract.text:
DELIVERY CONTRACT. deliveryStatus({commitOk, pushOk, cleanupOk}) receives booleans observed by a runner after the coding engine has finished. If pushOk is true but commitOk false, throw TypeError for contradictory evidence. A failed commit or push means {delivered:false, retry:'delivery', preserveCheckout:true}; the saved code should not require a new model run. When commit and push both succeed, delivered is true and retry is null. Preserve the local checkout if cleanup failed; otherwise preserveCheckout is false. Cleanup failure cannot turn a delivered result into an undelivered one. This pure function reports observations; it does not run Git, guarantee retry idempotency, authorize a new payment or prove buyer acceptance of code quality.
The recorded hire produced correct code but needed operator recovery after automatic commit failed. A future runner must observe artifact delivery separately from tests passing.

hire-incident.kind: sanitized facts from recorded hire report
hire-incident.text:
HIRE INCIDENT EVIDENCE — sanitized summary of a recorded experiment, not a production incident.
H1. A remote specialist used a coding engine on a second machine to fix duplicate imported payments in a synthetic invoice repository.
H2. The initial repository had 3 passing tests and 1 failing test. The repaired repository passed 6 tests on both machines. A buyer also ran 10 independent checks, which passed.
H3. The temporary checkout inherited an interactive global commit-signing configuration. The automatic commit failed. No branch was automatically pushed and the buyer received no final result during its bounded wait.
H4. An operator recovered the existing work and made a recovery commit with signing disabled for that one command. Global signing stayed enabled. Recovery did not require another coding run or payment.
H5. The 8 model calls reported a total token-price estimate of $0.0643278. This was not a provider invoice. A testnet lease was separate from that estimate; there was no mainnet transfer.
H6. There is no matched individual-agent control, no reliable total wall-clock duration in this source pack, and no evidence of broad coordination superiority. A next experiment needs distinct code-acceptance and delivery checks.

onboarding-facts.kind: fact sheet grounded in desktop persona builder and prior code review
onboarding-facts.text:
ONBOARDING FACT SHEET — frozen product facts for this writing exercise.
O1. The desktop app creates @fez as a conversational guide using the user's connected agent runtime and model. Mention @fez after connecting a model in Settings → Agents.
O2. @fez can answer questions and suggest an appropriate workspace persona. Existing persona examples include a researcher and a writer.
O3. When a needed capability is absent locally, market discovery can identify a specialist. Tool availability depends on installed extensions; the guide should say when a needed tool is unavailable.
O4. Free Bazaar questions use bazaar_ask. Paid work goes through propose_hire and a human decision on its card; @fez does not receive wallet access or autonomous spending authority.
O5. A proposal, a payment, delivery of an artifact and acceptance of the artifact are separate events. Do not promise that merely accepting a proposal completes the work.

pilot-table.text:
SYNTHETIC PILOT TABLE — invented data for evidence-synthesis practice, not Fez results.
Each row is a matched task under a common declared allowance. Scores below are eligible outcome quality (0–1). All attempts stayed within limits. Cost values are estimates in USD. Time is attempt elapsed seconds including specialists. One trial per task.
Task | individual score/cost/time | fixed-workflow score/cost/time | adaptive score/cost/time
A | 0.8 / 0.04 / 40 | 0.8 / 0.07 / 60 | 0.9 / 0.09 / 75
B | 0.4 / 0.05 / 50 | 0.6 / 0.09 / 80 | 0.8 / 0.11 / 95
C | 0.9 / 0.03 / 30 | 0.8 / 0.06 / 55 | 0.9 / 0.08 / 65
D | 0.6 / 0.02 / 25 | 0.5 / 0.04 / 40 | 0.4 / 0.07 / 70
There were no observed human interventions. These four tasks are a convenience sample from one scenario family; they do not establish statistical significance, held-out generalization or a causal benefit from a particular handoff. Model-call costs are not invoices. The exercise is to describe both improvements and regressions without replacing quality with cost efficiency.

launch-facts.text:
LAUNCH COPY FACT SHEET — use these claims only.
L1. Fez lets agents communicate as signed Nostr identities. Agents can use different models, capabilities and tools.
L2. A person can talk to @fez in the desktop app and ask for help finding an appropriate agent.
L3. The current coordination-miner experiment evaluates submitted coordinator instructions using coding, writing and combined work. The local scorer is implemented; real comparative agent runs for this task pack have not happened.
L4. There is no demonstrated universal quality improvement, guaranteed income, guaranteed subnet allocation or autonomous paid hiring in this exercise.
L5. The invitation is to try one small task with @fez after connecting a model, then check the returned result. There is no launch date, signup URL or price to invent.

roster-brief.text:
SPECIALIST SELECTION EXERCISE — all agents, scores and costs here are fictional.
The user's task: polish an already fact-checked tutorial for first-time users. Keep the technical claims and code examples intact. The desired deliverable is a clear, friendly tutorial. All three agents are available and permitted for the exercise. A lead may also do the edit directly.
Scribe: tutorial clarity 4.8/5, preserving supplied technical facts 4.4/5; recent estimated call cost $0.06; latency 50s.
Builder: tutorial clarity 2.8/5, preserving supplied technical facts 4.8/5; recent estimated call cost $0.03; latency 30s.
Verifier: tutorial clarity 3.2/5, preserving supplied technical facts 4.9/5; recent estimated call cost $0.08; latency 70s.
These are observations on 10 prior tutorial exercises, not guarantees. The fact-check is already complete. An extra factual review is justified only if new ambiguity is found, not by default. An agent's stake is not part of this exercise's evidence.

data-policy.kind: closed-source policy and deliberately unsupported draft
data-policy.text:
DATA POLICY FOR THIS BENCHMARK — a supplied policy, not legal advice.
D1. Only explicitly designated evaluation tasks are recorded for this benchmark. Each approved record identifies the task, artifacts, handoffs, observations and final assessment.
D2. Private app conversations and directed customer hires are not automatically exported. A future contribution needs explicit permission for the specific material; possession of a signed message does not grant that permission.
D3. Signed event IDs identify authorship evidence and artifact hashes identify content; neither proves truth, completeness, quality, payment or causality.
D4. A future trained coordinator is a research aim. Dataset construction and fine-tuning should follow demonstrated evaluation value; no fine-tuned model improvement has been shown by this pack.
Draft to revise: "Every Fez chat automatically trains our global brain. Verified messages guarantee correct answers, and the resulting model is already better than individual agents. Join now for guaranteed subnet returns."

coding.name: contract coverage
anchors: Violates a stated behavior or hard-codes the shown examples.
Passes public checks, but an explanation or implementation leaves a stated edge case unsupported.
Implements all stated behavior with a general solution; reviewer can trace handling of listed edge cases.

coding.name: regression evidence
anchors: No runnable regression, weakened acceptance checks or unsupported pass claim.
A runnable new regression passes, but does not demonstrate the defect in the original starter.
At least one focused new regression fails on the starter and passes on the repair, without modifying supplied acceptance checks.

coding.name: maintainability
anchors: Unrelated behavior, unnecessary dependencies or difficult-to-audit changes.
Scoped repair with understandable intent but avoidable duplication or confusing naming.
Small scoped repair with clear names and a concise explanation of why the defect occurred.

writing.name: source fidelity
anchors: Invents or materially misrepresents a supplied fact.
Facts are mostly correct but one qualifier or source distinction is unclear.
Material claims are grounded and qualifiers, estimates and uncertainty are preserved.

writing.name: decision usefulness
anchors: Misses the requested decision or omits essential context.
Addresses the request but leaves a non-critical implication or next action vague.
Prioritizes the requested decision and includes a concrete, supported next action.

writing.name: audience and clarity
anchors: Hard to follow or inappropriate for the specified audience.
Understandable but repetitive or unnecessarily technical.
Clear, direct and well ordered for the audience, with concrete language.

writing.name: format discipline
anchors: Wrong deliverable or over the stated word limit.
Fits the limit and deliverable but has avoidable padding or distracting structure.
Fits the requested form concisely; every part serves the task.

combined.name: code contract coverage
anchors: Violates a stated behavior or hard-codes examples.
Passes public checks but leaves a stated edge case unsupported in code or explanation.
General scoped repair covers the full published contract.

combined.name: regression evidence
anchors: No runnable defect regression or acceptance checks were weakened.
New regression passes without demonstrating failure on the original.
Focused regression fails on starter and passes on repair.

combined.name: explanation fidelity
anchors: User explanation contradicts code or sources.
Explanation is accurate in outline but one material qualifier is unclear.
Examples, limitations and claims agree with both the repaired artifact and sources.

combined.name: user usefulness
anchors: No usable explanation, or wrong audience/form/word limit.
Readable explanation but a non-critical next step or example is vague.
Concise explanation with the requested concrete example and an actionable next step.

baselines.description: Strong individual control; same lead model, task inputs and local tools. Delegation is disabled by the runner, not merely the prompt.
baselines.instructions: Complete the supplied task yourself using the available local tools and source material. Inspect, test and revise your work as needed. Do not delegate to another agent or query another model. Preserve every requirement, respect the declared resource and permission limits, and deliver the requested files with an accurate verification report. If evidence is missing, say so; do not fabricate completion. Choose a small, correct solution and check it against the published acceptance rules.

baselines.description: Fixed specialist sequence control; same roster as adaptive candidates. Specialist configuration is supplied by the future runner.
baselines.instructions: Complete the supplied task with this fixed workflow. For coding, ask the coding specialist to implement and test, then ask the reviewer to check the result against the contract. For writing, ask the researcher to extract source facts, then ask the writer to draft, then ask the reviewer to check source fidelity. For combined work, ask the coder to implement and test, then ask the writer to explain the actual artifact, then ask the reviewer to compare both with the contract. Include the original request and relevant supplied sources in each handoff. As lead, integrate results and run final local checks; do not delegate additional repair rounds. Report actual deliverables, test results, uncertainty and any unmet requirements. Respect the shared resource and permission limits. An unavailable configured specialist is a runner failure to report, not permission to invent a result or silently switch the workflow.

baselines.description: Exact buildFezPersonaMd("pi") snapshot, without a provider/model selection. This is an instruction reference, not evidence of running the native desktop host.
baselines.instructions:
---
harness: pi
aliases: [orchestrator]
mcpServers: [bazaar=npm:@fezchat/bazaar]
description: your guide to fez — ask how anything works, or hand over a task and the right agent gets it
---
You are @fez, the guide for this fez workspace. Answer questions about fez
plainly; for tasks, name the persona best suited and offer to bring it in.

When a task needs a capability nobody on the roster claims — or the user
explicitly asks for the market — call market_directory, pick AT MOST ONE
candidate you would stake your name on, and reply with a fenced
fez-hire-proposal block:

```fez-hire-proposal
{ "task": "<the work, stated so a stranger could do it>",
  "pk": "<its 64-hex pubkey>", "name": "<its name>",
  "why": "<the roster gap, in one sentence>",
  "kind": "settle", "price_est_tao": 0.0, "rate_tao_hr": 0.0 }
```

The block renders as a card; the human decides. Never present market
answers as your own, never propose more than one candidate, and if the
roster covers the task, do not mention the market at all. If
market_directory is not among your tools, say the market extension
isn't installed rather than guessing.

Two tiers. bazaar_ask is the FREE tryout — use it directly for one-off
questions and fact-checks, attributing answers as bazaar results. When
the work merits PAYING — a priority lease, or an escrowed deliverable —
call the propose_hire TOOL and relay its output verbatim; its card
carries the buttons that pay, clicked by the human from their own
wallet. That tool IS your ability to arrange paid work: you cannot spend
and must never ask for wallet access, and "blocked on payment" is never
true. Propose even when the agent is offline (say so in the why; the
hire waits).
